places.title: Speicherstadt
places.why: The largest historic warehouse district in the world: long rows of red-brick warehouses with Gothic Revival gables and turrets, built on oak piles between narrow canals and crossed by iron bridges. It was built for the free port after Hamburg joined the German customs union.
places.note: The map shows the canals (Fleete) that run through the Speicherstadt; OpenStreetMap has no outline of the district.

places.title: Chilehaus and the Kontorhaus District
places.architect: Fritz Höger; Hans and Oskar Gerson
places.why: A district of large office buildings of the 1920s and 1930s, all in dark clinker brick. The Chilehaus ends in a sharp corner like a ship's bow, its facade rippling with brick piers; the Sprinkenhof and the Meßberghof next to it show the same brick expressionism on a grid of piers and patterned bricks.

places.title: Elbphilharmonie
places.why: A glass superstructure with a roof like breaking waves, set on a brick quay warehouse of the 1960s at the tip of a pier between the river and the city. A long curved escalator leads up to the Plaza, a public terrace running around the building between the old and the new parts.

places.title: HafenCity
places.architect: Masterplan KCAP and ASTOC; public spaces EMBT and WES
places.why: A new city district on the former docks south of the Speicherstadt, one of the largest inner-city developments in Europe. The buildings stand on raised plinths above flood level, while promenades, pontoons and stepped squares such as the Magellan and Marco Polo Terraces lead down to the water.
places.note: The outline is the HafenCity quarter boundary, which also takes in the Speicherstadt.

places.title: Rathaus, Rathausmarkt and Alster Arcades
places.why: A Neo-Renaissance city hall with a 112-metre tower and a facade lined with statues of emperors, facing the city's main square. The Stock Exchange is joined to its back, and across the square the white Alster Arcades run along the water of the Alster canal.

places.title: St. Michaelis (Michel)
places.architect: Johann Leonhard Prey and Ernst Georg Sonnin
places.why: Hamburg's Baroque landmark church, with a 132-metre copper-topped tower and a viewing platform over the port and the city. The white and gold interior is a single wide hall with curved galleries.

photos.file: Hamburg, Hafen, Rickmer Rickmers und Michaeliskirche -- 2016 -- 3117.jpg
photos.author: Dietmar Rabich

places.title: St. Pauli Landungsbrücken and Old Elbe Tunnel
places.why: A long stone hall with copper domes and a clock tower in front of the floating piers where ferries and harbour boats land. In a domed building at its west end, lifts carry people and cars down to the Old Elbe Tunnel of 1911, two tiled tubes under the river.

photos.file: Zentraler Blick durch den Alten Elbtunnel.jpg
photos.author: GZagatta

places.title: Binnenalster and Jungfernstieg
places.architect: Jungfernstieg redesign: André Poitiers with WES
places.why: A square lake in the heart of the city with a tall fountain, framed by hotels, offices and the spires of the old town. Its south shore, the Jungfernstieg, is a promenade with broad steps down to the water and the landing of the Alster boats.

places.title: Außenalster
places.why: A large lake in the middle of the city, ringed by a path of about seven kilometres, lawns and white villas. On fine days it fills with sailing boats, canoes and rowers, with the skyline of church spires at its south end.

places.title: Reeperbahn and Spielbudenplatz
places.why: St. Pauli's mile of theatres, music clubs and bars, on the strip where ropemakers once twisted ship's ropes outside the city walls. Spielbudenplatz beside it is an open square used for markets and concerts.

places.title: Fischmarkt and Fish Auction Hall
places.why: A riverside square that has held a market since 1703, next to the Fish Auction Hall of 1896: an iron-and-glass hall in the form of a three-aisled basilica, built for the Altona fishing fleet and restored in the 1980s.

places.title: Planten un Blomen
places.architect: Karl Plomin and others; redesign POLA
places.why: A chain of gardens on the old city ramparts, from the Old Botanical Garden with its glasshouses to a large Japanese garden, rose gardens and a lake with fountains. A recent redesign opened the park towards the Dag-Hammarskjöld-Platz and the Marseiller Promenade.

places.title: St. Nikolai Memorial
places.why: The 147-metre Gothic Revival spire of a main church, briefly the tallest building in the world, stands over the burnt-out walls of the nave as a memorial to the victims of the 1943 air raids. A glass lift goes up to a viewing platform in the tower.

places.title: Sternschanze (Schanzenviertel)
places.why: A dense quarter of 19th-century tenements around the Schulterblatt, with cafés spilling onto the pavements and independent shops. Its centre is the Rote Flora, a theatre of 1888 that has been occupied as a social centre since 1989.
places.note: The outline is the Sternschanze quarter boundary.

places.title: Övelgönne and the Elbe beach
places.why: A footpath of small captains' and pilots' houses with front gardens along the Elbe, with a sandy beach below where container ships pass close by. At its east end, old ships of the museum harbour lie moored at a pontoon.

places.title: St. Petri
places.architect: Alexis de Chateauneuf and Hermann Peter Fersenfeldt
places.why: The oldest parish church of the city, rebuilt in Gothic Revival brick on its medieval plan after the Great Fire of 1842. Its slender green spire, which can be climbed, is one of the five main church towers of the skyline.

photos.file: St. Petri am Domplatz in Hamburg.jpg
photos.author: Pauli-Pirat

places.title: Bunker St. Pauli (Flak Tower IV)
places.why: A massive concrete anti-aircraft tower of 1942, raised by five storeys and planted with trees and shrubs. A public path winds up around the new levels to a roof garden with views over the Heiligengeistfeld and the city.

photos.file: HH-St.-Pauli Saisonabschluss der STP 1.C vs RSC 2.C vor dem Flak-Bunker, Jun 2025.jpg
photos.author: An-d

places.title: Jarrestadt
places.why: A housing estate of about 1,800 flats in red-brick blocks with flat roofs, built on a plan by Karl Schneider under the city architect Fritz Schumacher. Ten architects designed the blocks around large green courtyards and a central green strip.

places.title: Treppenviertel, Blankenese
places.why: A former fishing and pilots' village on the steep bank of the Elbe, where captains' houses and cottages are reached only by a maze of stairways and narrow paths leading down to the river beach.

places.title: Krameramtsstuben
places.why: A narrow courtyard of half-timbered row houses built in the 17th century by the shopkeepers' guild for the widows of its members, the last ensemble of its kind in the city centre.

places.title: Neue Hamburger Terrassen
places.architect: LAN Architecture (masterplan and 33 houses); hauschild + siegel and others
places.why: A small quarter from the IBA 2013 building exhibition that reinterprets the Hamburg terrace, the working-class row house of the 19th century. Timber-clad blocks with row houses and flats face each other across a narrow green street, with shared courtyards behind.

places.title: Roots
places.why: The tallest timber high-rise in Germany, about 65 metres, with flats built of solid wooden walls and floors, on the Baakenhafen in eastern HafenCity.

places.title: Cinnamon Tower and Old Harbour Office
places.why: A slim residential tower beside the restored brick harbour master's office and a small pavilion, a deliberate contrast in scale to the large blocks of the Überseequartier around it.

photos.file: HafenCity Altes Hafenamt Osaka-Allee 14 Eingang Markt.JPG
photos.author: OldfashionFreak

places.title: Hamburger Kunsthalle
places.architect: Hermann von der Hude and Georg Theodor Schirrmacher; Fritz Schumacher and Albert Erbe; O. M. Ungers
places.why: Three buildings from three eras: a red-brick hall in Italian Renaissance style, a domed extension finished in 1919, and the Galerie der Gegenwart, a white cube on a granite plinth built on a strict square grid by O. M. Ungers.

places.title: Empire Riverside Hotel
places.why: A slim 20-storey hotel tower clad in bronze-coloured aluminium, standing on a low base on the slope above the harbour; the bar on the top floor looks out over the port.

places.title: Unilever House and Marco Polo Tower
places.why: Two buildings by the same architects on the Strandkai: an office house wrapped in a transparent foil skin around a tall open atrium with a public ground floor, and a 17-storey residential tower whose floors are twisted against each other, each with a deep terrace.

places.title: Dockland
places.why: An office building shaped like a ship's bow, projecting 40 metres out over the Elbe at the ferry terminal of the old fishing port. Public outdoor stairs climb its sloping back to a roof terrace with a view of the port.

places.title: Spiegel Building and Ericusspitze
places.why: The news magazine's headquarters at the tip of the Ericus peninsula: a glass block with a large cut-out opening towards the water and the Speicherstadt. In front of it, a square with a pool flush with the paving reflects the facades.

places.title: Finanzbehörde
places.why: The finance office on the Gänsemarkt by the city architect Fritz Schumacher, a large block of dark clinker brick with patterned brickwork and terracotta ornament, a key work of Hamburg's brick architecture of the 1920s.

places.title: Museum für Hamburgische Geschichte
places.architect: Fritz Schumacher; courtyard roof gmp with Jörg Schlaich
places.why: A brick museum by Fritz Schumacher on the old city ramparts, with portals and fragments of demolished city buildings built into its walls. Its inner courtyard is covered by a light glass grid shell added in 1989.

places.title: Heinrich-Hertz-Turm
places.why: A 279-metre concrete telecommunications tower by Fritz Trautwein and the engineer Fritz Leonhardt, the tallest structure in Hamburg, rising next to Planten un Blomen. Its viewing levels have been closed since 2001.

photos.author: Tony Webster from Portland, Oregon, United States

places.title: Deichstraße and Nikolaifleet
places.why: The last street of old merchants' houses in the city centre: tall, narrow houses of the 17th to 19th centuries that face the street at the front and the Nikolaifleet canal at the back, where goods were once loaded from boats.

places.title: Wilhelmsburg Mitte (IBA 2013)
places.why: The showcase of the IBA 2013 building exhibition. Its centre is the ministry of urban development, a curved office building clad in bands of coloured glazed ceramic that rises to a tower; nearby, Woodie is a student hall of 371 prefabricated timber modules.

places.title: Jugendmusikschule
places.why: A music school for young people whose curved, sinuous volumes are fitted between the old trees of the site and the existing buildings around it. Inside, the full-height hall and a stepped ramp link the public rooms with the classrooms.

places.title: Elbbrücken Station
places.why: Metro and suburban rail stations under long roofs of steel and glass whose diagonal structure echoes the trusses of the neighbouring Elbe bridges; a glazed skywalk links the two.

places.title: BallinStadt
places.why: Brick halls rebuilt on the site of the emigrant halls where millions of people waited before sailing to America; the museum tells their stories.

places.title: St. Katharinen
places.why: A Gothic brick hall church of merchants and brewers by the Speicherstadt, with a Baroque tower top of 1657 crowned in gold. It was rebuilt after the war.

places.title: ADA1 (An der Alster 1)
places.why: An office building on the shore of the Außenalster with a facade of white horizontal bands that swell into large oval eyes, deeper spaces in its double skin that look out over the lake.

places.title: The Fontenay
places.why: A hotel on the shore of the Außenalster made of three overlapping circles, its white curved facades opening to the lake and the park.

photos.file: The Fontenay Hamburg Hotel pre-opening phase in march 2018.jpg
photos.author: Bildforyou7

places.title: Landhaus Michaelsen
places.why: An early modernist country house high above the Elbe beach at Falkenstein: a white composition of cubes with a large curved window towards the river, its sloping roof following the line of the hills.

places.title: Old Ferry Terminal Altona
places.why: A long steel and glass building on the Elbe quay, built as a ferry and cruise terminal with offices above, one of the first new buildings on the Altona riverbank after the port moved away.

places.title: Montblanc Haus
places.why: A 100-metre exhibition building on the art of writing next to the pen maker's factory, with a main facade of black textured concrete and a top-lit foyer inside.

places.title: Berliner Bogen
places.why: An office building under a 36-metre parabolic steel arch, built over a stormwater basin; office floors and glazed winter gardens sit inside one curved glass skin.

places.title: Großmarkthalle and Mehr! Theater
places.why: The wholesale market hall of 1962, a long hall roofed by a row of thin concrete waves. One part now houses a theatre, entered through a new foyer pavilion by Carmody Groarke.

places.title: Alsterschwimmhalle
places.architect: Horst Niessen, Rolf Störmer, Walter Neuhäusser; renovation gmp
places.why: Known as the swimming opera: a pool hall under two hyperbolic paraboloid concrete shells resting on three points, designed with the engineer Jörg Schlaich. A recent renovation by gmp kept the roof and added a new diving pool and entrance building.

places.title: Köhlbrandbrücke
places.why: A cable-stayed bridge in the middle of the port, rising high over the Köhlbrand channel on two A-shaped pylons, its curved approach ramps a landmark of the harbour skyline.

places.title: Energiebunker
places.why: A wartime flak bunker, left as a ruin after it was partly blown up in 1947, rebuilt for the IBA 2013 as a renewable energy plant with a solar facade and a café and terrace on the roof.

places.title: St. Maximilian Kolbe
places.why: A former Catholic church of exposed concrete and yellow brick built in a spiral, so that its walls and the tower wind upwards; it was restored and turned into a community centre in 2022.

places.title: Stadtpark and Planetarium
places.why: A large people's park laid out on a straight axis from the old water tower, now the Planetarium, across a great lawn to a lake with an open-air pool, with rose and rock gardens and a beer garden on the side.

places.title: Altonaer Volkspark
places.why: Hamburg's largest park, a woodland people's park laid out from 1914 with walking paths, meadows and show gardens such as a large dahlia garden.

places.title: Lohsepark
places.why: The largest green space in HafenCity, a long lawn framed by tree-lined promenades and planted with old fruit varieties; within it a memorial marks the Hannoverscher Bahnhof, from which Jews, Sinti and Roma were deported.

places.title: Baakenpark
places.why: A park on an artificial peninsula in the Baakenhafen basin, with a 15-metre grassy hill, play terraces and wild shorelines on several levels.

photos.file: Baakenpark HafenCity Blick vom Himmelsberg auf den Park.jpg
photos.author: Pauli-Pirat

photos.file: Baakenpark HafenCity Sitzpodeste und spätere Schaukeln.jpg
photos.author: Pauli-Pirat

places.title: Jenischpark
places.architect: Caspar Voght; Jenisch Haus by Franz Gustav Forsmann
places.why: Hamburg's oldest landscape park, sloping down to the Elbe, with the Neoclassical Jenisch Haus and the Ernst Barlach Haus among old trees and meadows.

places.title: Hirschpark
places.why: A former estate park on the high bank of the Elbe, with an old avenue of lime trees, a deer enclosure and the white Hirschparkhaus.

places.title: Wilhelmsburger Inselpark
places.why: The park of the 2013 International Garden Show on the Elbe island of Wilhelmsburg, with lakes, themed gardens, sports halls and Hamburg's largest skate park.

places.title: Harburger Stadtpark
places.why: A people's park of the 1920s around the Außenmühlenteich lake, a protected garden monument with paths around the water.

photos.file: Harburger Stadtpark in Hamburg-Wilstorf Ufergestaltung am Nordende (2).jpg
photos.author: Pauli-Pirat

photos.file: Harburger Stadtpark in Hamburg-Wilstorf Ufergestaltung am Nordende (1).jpg
photos.author: Pauli-Pirat

places.title: Bergedorf Castle and Castle Garden
places.why: Hamburg's only castle, a moated brick building in Bergedorf, with old trees in the small landscape garden around it.

photos.file: RK 2203 Bergedorfer Schloss von der Serrahnbrücke P1870882.jpg
photos.author: Reinhard Kraasch

places.title: Innocentiapark
places.why: A green square park among the villas and apartment houses of Harvestehude, with lawns and old trees.

places.title: Eimsbütteler Park Am Weiher
places.why: A neighbourhood park around a pond in Eimsbüttel, on the site of an old wood that was a traditional excursion spot for Hamburg people.

places.title: Eichtalpark
places.why: A park along the Wandse valley with a historic gatehouse, old oaks and wide meadows, recently reworked as a climate park with a new floodplain.

places.title: Öjendorfer Park
places.why: The third-largest park in Hamburg, around a lake twice the size of the Binnenalster, used for swimming and picnics in summer.

places.title: Ohlsdorf Cemetery
places.why: One of the largest park cemeteries in the world, a landscape of lakes, avenues, rhododendrons and chapels. Fritz Schumacher's brick crematorium of 1932 stands near the main entrance.

places.title: Jan-Fedder-Promenade (Niederhafen)
places.why: The flood wall between Baumwall and the Landungsbrücken, raised and turned into a wide promenade with flowing concrete steps and terraces down to the harbour.

photos.file: Hamburg Port at summer evening, August 2025 1.jpg
photos.author: Karlheinz Klingbeil

places.title: Park Mitte Altona
places.why: A new park on former railway land at the heart of the Mitte Altona quarter, with a long open meadow, play areas and paths between the new housing blocks.
